To establish standardized procedures for the identification, traceability, safe handling, and reduction of hazardous substances and to ensure environmentally sound treatment and disposal.
This SOP applies to all Cherry Hill offices, warehouses, and project execution sites where hazardous substances are procured, stored, used, or disposed of.

body.text: All incoming materials are classified as hazardous, based on manufacturer provided Safety Data Sheets (SDS), GHS symbols, and chemical composition are entered into Cherry Hill’s central inventory system. Materials include but are not limited to:

High-VOC paints and adhesives
Flammable solvents
Chemical cleaners and degreasers
Batteries and spent electrical components

Each item is recorded with its unique barcode upon receipt, capturing the following details: batch/lot number, expiry date, storage location, and issuing department.

Each hazardous substance container is clearly labelled with the product name, hazard classification, GHS pictograms, handling precautions, storage requirements, and expiry date (where applicable). Damaged or illegible labels are replaced immediately to ensure safe identification and compliance throughout the material lifecycle.

All hazardous substances are stored in pre-designated enclosures fitted with ventilation systems, flame-proof panels, and spill containment trays. Incompatible chemicals are stored separately, and stock rotation is enforced based on expiry tracking. Only trained personnel are authorized to handle these substances, using appropriate PPE (e.g., gloves, respirators, goggles). Emergency response equipment such as eyewash stations, fire extinguishers, and spill kits are available at all relevant locations.

Hazardous substances are transported within office premises, warehouses, and project sites using sealed, compatible containers and suitable handling equipment to prevent spills, leaks, or accidental exposure. Containers remain properly labelled during transportation, and incompatible substances are never transported or stored together. Where materials are transported to or from project sites, transportation is carried out in accordance with applicable legal and safety requirements.

Cherry Hill maintains a systematic traceability process to monitor hazardous substances throughout their lifecycle—from procurement to final disposal. Upon receipt, each hazardous material is assigned a unique identification code or barcode and recorded in the inventory management system along with details such as supplier name, purchase order number, batch/lot number, manufacturing and expiry dates, storage location, quantity received, and Safety Data Sheet (SDS) reference.

Whenever hazardous substances are issued for use at project sites or within office and warehouse operations, the quantity issued, receiving department or project, date of issue, and responsible employee are recorded in the material issue register or digital inventory system. Any returned, unused, expired, or damaged materials are similarly documented to maintain complete accountability and inventory accuracy.

Hazardous waste generated during project execution is labelled with the waste type, source location, date of generation, and temporary storage location before being transferred to the designated hazardous waste storage area. Waste movement records are maintained until collection by an authorised waste management agency, ensuring complete traceability through waste manifests, transporter details, and disposal certificates.

Periodic inventory reconciliation and internal inspections are carried out to verify stock balances, storage conditions, barcode records, and disposal documentation. Any discrepancies identified during inspections are investigated promptly, corrective actions are implemented, and records are retained to demonstrate compliance with regulatory requirements and company procedures.
Where feasible, Cherry Hill prioritizes substitution of hazardous materials with eco-labeled or low-toxicity alternatives. Examples include:

Water-based paints and sealants in place of solvent-based options
Mechanical fixing systems that reduce adhesive dependency
Reusable cleaning tools instead of chemical-intensive cleaners

Design teams collaborate with procurement to identify less hazardous options without compromising functionality or finish standards. Controlled dispensing units and pre-measured packaging are employed to reduce material wastage during application, particularly in painting and polishing works.

Procurement teams also evaluate suppliers offering environmentally preferable products with lower hazardous content, while project teams optimize material planning to avoid over-ordering and unnecessary chemical waste generation. Wherever practical, reusable containers, refill systems, and bulk purchasing are adopted to minimise packaging waste and reduce the overall generation of hazardous waste.

Cherry Hill ensures that hazardous substances and hazardous waste are managed safely throughout their lifecycle to prevent adverse impacts on employees, the public, and the environment. Disposal activities are carried out in accordance with applicable legal requirements and through authorised service providers.

substeps.text: Identification and Assessment: Hazardous substances that are expired, damaged, contaminated, or no longer required, along with hazardous waste generated during project execution, maintenance, or office operations, are identified by the responsible department. The HSSE Team assesses whether the material can be safely reused, returned to the supplier, recycled, recovered, or requires specialised treatment and disposal.

Safe Collection and Temporary Storage: Hazardous substances awaiting treatment or disposal, and hazardous waste such as solvent residues, paint containers, adhesive containers, contaminated absorbents, chemical cleaners, batteries, fluorescent lamps, and electronic components, are collected separately from general waste. All containers are properly sealed, labelled with the contents and hazard classification, and stored in designated hazardous material storage areas equipped with spill containment, ventilation, and restricted access until collection.

Specialized Treatment: Where specialised treatment is required, Cherry Hill ensures that hazardous substances or waste are transferred only to authorised facilities capable of carrying out appropriate treatment processes, including recycling, recovery, neutralisation, or other environmentally sound treatment methods, depending on the nature of the material. Whenever feasible, unused hazardous substances are returned to the supplier under take-back programmes or sent to authorised recycling or recovery facilities to minimise disposal.

Transportation and Final Disposal: Hazardous substances and hazardous waste are transported only by authorised transporters using suitable containers and packaging to prevent leaks, spills, or accidental exposure during transit. Final treatment and disposal are carried out exclusively by government-authorised Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facilities (TSDFs) or licensed hazardous waste management agencies in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

Documentation and Verification: The HSSE Team maintains records of hazardous substances and waste sent for treatment or disposal, including inventory details, quantities, transporter information, waste manifests, treatment or recycling certificates, and disposal records. These records are periodically reviewed to verify complete traceability, regulatory compliance, and identify opportunities to reduce the use and disposal of hazardous substances.

blocks.text: Field staff, site supervisors, and warehouse teams undergo annual training on chemical safety, emergency response, waste handling, and the digital traceability platform. Safety drills and toolbox talks reinforce key precautions and promote proactive incident reporting culture.

The HSSE Team reviews this SOP annually, or earlier if material changes are introduced in operations, materials, or legislation. Review includes evaluation of material usage reports, Feedback from project teams, Incident logs and regulatory updates. Recommended improvements are formally documented and implemented following leadership approval.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes Cherry Hill Interiors Pvt. Ltd.'s approach to managing waste generated during office operations, warehouse activities, and project execution. It provides a structured process for reducing waste generation, promoting material reuse and recycling, ensuring proper segregation, and supporting environmentally responsible disposal practices in compliance with applicable legal requirements.

This SOP applies to all Cherry Hill offices, warehouses, fabrication areas, and project sites where waste is generated through construction, interior fit-out, maintenance, logistics, and administrative activities.
It applies to all employees, contractors, subcontractors, and service providers working under Cherry Hill's operational control.

responsibilities: Monitors implementation of waste management practices, conducts inspections, and maintains waste management records.
Ensures waste segregation, housekeeping, material reuse, recycling, and disposal activities are effectively implemented at project sites.
Segregate waste into designated waste streams, use the assigned collection points, and maintain good housekeeping practices.

body.text: Waste streams are identified during project planning and throughout project execution to ensure appropriate waste handling and disposal methods are implemented.
The common waste streams generated across Cherry Hill operations include:

Concrete debris
Cement bags
Gypsum board off-cuts
Timber and plywood
Wooden pallets
Metal scrap and aluminium sections
Glass off-cuts
Electrical cables and MEP materials
Paper and cardboard
Plastic bottles and packaging materials
Used paint containers
Food waste
General municipal waste
The identified waste streams are reviewed periodically whenever project activities, materials, or construction methods change to ensure suitable waste management arrangements remain effective.
Cherry Hill follows the waste hierarchy by prioritising Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, and Responsible Disposal during all project activities.
Waste generation is reduced through careful planning of material quantities, controlled procurement, proper storage, and efficient utilisation of construction materials.
Project teams minimise waste by:

Procuring materials according to approved Bills of Quantities (BOQs) and project schedules.
Scheduling material deliveries in phases to prevent excess storage and material deterioration.
Protecting materials from moisture, physical damage, and contamination through designated storage arrangements.
Optimising cutting plans for gypsum boards, laminates, veneers, ceiling tiles, aluminium sections, and glass panels to minimise off-cuts.
Monitoring material consumption against project progress to identify excessive wastage.
Encouraging suppliers to provide reusable pallets, returnable packaging, and recyclable materials wherever practical.
Material wastage is reviewed during routine site coordination meetings, and improvement opportunities are identified where abnormal consumption trends are observed.

steps.heading: Reduction of Internal Waste through Material Reuse, Recovery and Repurposing

body.text: Before any material is classified as waste, it is assessed to determine whether it can be reused, repaired, recovered, or repurposed within Cherry Hill operations.

Reusable materials are segregated from the general waste stream and stored in designated reuse areas within the warehouse or project site. Where necessary, materials are cleaned, repaired, trimmed, or refurbished before being returned to operational use.
Typical reuse and repurposing practices include:

Timber, plywood, and wooden boards are reused for temporary site protection, barricading, storage platforms, and access pathways.
Wooden pallets are reused for stacking and protecting construction materials within warehouses and project sites.
Metal sections and aluminium off-cuts are repurposed for temporary supports, brackets, and fabrication works.
Reusable formwork is inspected, repaired where required, and reused for subsequent construction activities.
Empty drums and containers are reused for temporary storage of non-hazardous materials where safe and appropriate.
Surplus gypsum boards, ceiling tiles, laminates, veneers, and flooring materials that remain in usable condition are retained for future project requirements, sample installations, or mock-up works.
Organic waste generated from pantry facilities is directed for composting where practical.
Where internal reuse is not feasible, suitable materials are evaluated for recovery or recycling through authorised recycling agencies before disposal is considered.

steps.heading: Internal Sorting and Segregation of Waste

body.text: Waste generated during office operations, warehouse activities, and project execution is segregated immediately at the point of generation according to the designated waste streams.
Colour-coded waste collection bins are provided across project sites and offices to facilitate effective segregation:

Green Bin – Food and organic waste
Blue Bin – Paper and cardboard
Yellow Bin – Plastic bottles, plastic wrapping, and polythene
Grey Bin – General municipal waste
Red Bin – Used paint containers and other hazardous waste (where applicable)
Dedicated collection areas are also maintained for:

Metal scrap and aluminium sections
Timber and wooden pallets
Concrete debris
Electrical cables
Reusable construction materials
Waste is placed only in the designated containers to prevent cross-contamination between waste streams.

Site Supervisors conduct daily housekeeping inspections to verify that waste segregation practices are being followed. Mixed waste identified during inspections is re-segregated before being transferred for reuse, recycling, or disposal. Housekeeping observations are discussed during toolbox talks to reinforce proper waste management practices.

steps.heading: Provision of Accessible Waste Collection Points

body.text: Waste collection points are established throughout project sites, warehouses, offices, and fabrication areas to facilitate efficient waste segregation and recycling.
Collection points are strategically located at areas where waste generation is highest, including:

Gypsum board and laminate cutting stations.
Carpentry and fabrication work areas.
Material unloading and storage locations.
Packaging and unpacking areas.
Warehouse operations.
Pantry and welfare facilities.
General work areas within project sites.
Each waste collection point includes clearly labelled colour-coded bins and signage indicating the acceptable waste category for each container.

Collection points are inspected daily to ensure they remain clean, accessible, and adequately sized for the volume of waste generated. Bins are emptied before reaching full capacity, and damaged containers or missing labels are replaced promptly.

As project activities progress, waste collection points are relocated where necessary to maintain easy access for employees and subcontractors and to encourage consistent recycling practices throughout the project lifecycle.
Materials that cannot be reused internally are segregated and transferred to authorised recycling agencies.

Typical recyclable materials include paper, cardboard, plastics, packaging materials, metal scrap, electrical cables, wooden pallets, and cement bags. Supplier take-back programmes for pallets and packaging materials are utilised wherever available.
Records of recyclable materials, including quantities and collection details, are maintained to monitor recycling performance.
Waste that cannot be reduced, reused, recovered, or recycled is disposed of through authorised waste management agencies in accordance with applicable statutory and environmental requirements.
Prior to disposal, waste is reviewed to ensure that all practical opportunities for reuse, recovery, or recycling have been considered.

Waste designated for disposal is temporarily stored in identified waste storage areas until collection. Storage areas are maintained in a clean and orderly condition to prevent littering, water contamination, and wind-blown waste.
Waste disposal practices include:

Food waste is directed to composting facilities where available.
Non-recyclable packaging materials are returned to suppliers wherever feasible or disposed of through authorised waste contractors.
Concrete debris is transported to approved disposal locations.
Used paint containers are returned to suppliers where applicable or disposed of through authorised municipal or licensed waste management agencies.
General municipal waste is collected by the authorised municipal collection service.
Waste transfer records, collection receipts, recycling certificates, and disposal documentation are maintained to ensure traceability and demonstrate compliance with applicable legal requirements.
The HSSE Team conducts periodic inspections and internal audits to monitor waste segregation, housekeeping, recycling performance, contractor compliance, and disposal records.

Waste generation trends and recycling performance are reviewed periodically to identify opportunities for improving resource efficiency. Corrective actions arising from inspections or audits are tracked to completion and incorporated into future project improvements.

blocks.text: This SOP is reviewed annually or whenever significant changes occur in project activities, waste streams, or applicable legal requirements.

The review considers waste generation trends, reuse and recycling performance, inspection findings, feedback from project teams, and opportunities for continual improvement. Approved revisions are communicated to all relevant employees and contractors before implementation.

sops.title: Procedure for Compliance Approval of Sensitive Transactions

blocks.text: To define the steps for identifying, approving, documenting, and managing sensitive or high-risk transactions, such as gifts, travel, entertainment, charitable contributions, political donations, and procurement, that may pose ethical, legal, or reputational risks to Cherry Hill.

body.text: Determine if the transaction falls under sensitive categories or consult the Compliance Officer for clarification.

substeps.text: Categories include: gifts, entertainment, hospitality, travel, donations, political contributions, and major procurement.

body.text: Submit the transaction details to the Ethics & Compliance Officer in person or via email at ethics.compliance@cherryhill.in

substeps.text: Include: Purpose, context, parties involved, and estimated value. High-value or high-risk transactions require a formal approval request. Approval must be provided within 2 business days of submission.

body.text: Once approved, document the approval with all supporting notes or emails.

substeps.text: Approval records must be uploaded to the centralized digital repository or stored in the designated transaction folder.

body.text: All documentation including purpose, cost, participants, and approval evidence must accompany the expense report. Records must be retained for a minimum of five years in accordance with Cherry Hill’s record retention policy.

Conduct a post-approval review within 10 business days of the transaction to assess any potential conflict of interest or ethical risk. A short ethical review note must be submitted and filed with the transaction record.
Verify the transaction does not involve restricted items such as personal cash, checks, or gifts that breach anti-bribery laws.

blocks.text: The Sensitive Transaction Approval Procedure is reviewed annually by the Ethics & Compliance Officer to ensure continued effectiveness, relevance, and alignment with applicable legal, regulatory, and corporate governance standards. Reviews may also be triggered immediately following any compliance breach or audit observation. Feedback from key departments such as Finance, Legal, and Procurement is incorporated to ensure the procedure remains practical and risk-sensitive. All updates are documented with version history and communicated to relevant stakeholders, with final approval resting with Senior Management and the Compliance Committee.

sops.title: Procedure for Confidential Data Handling and Breach Responses

blocks.text: To establish guidelines for classifying, protecting, and managing confidential information, including response procedures for data breaches and measures to secure third-party data against unauthorized access or disclosure at Cherry Hill.

body.text: Data Classification: Data must be classified into three categories:

rows: Highly sensitive (e.g., personal data, client data, financial information).
Internal use only (e.g., employee records, project documentation).
Non-sensitive information (e.g., marketing materials, published case studies).

body.text: Access Control:

Access rights are assigned based on the principle of least privilege. The principle of least privilege (PoLP) refers to granting users only the access rights necessary to perform their job functions, minimizing the risk of unauthorized access or data breaches.
Roles and responsibilities are defined, and access is granted accordingly.
A quarterly review of access rights will be conducted by Data Protection Officer through automated access logs and reports, along with manual checks to ensure compliance with the established classifications. In case of non-compliance, access rights will be revoked, investigated, and corrective actions will be implemented, followed by a follow-up review to ensure compliance.

Confidential information are stored in secure environments e.g., locked file cabinets and secure servers such as cloud-based servers to guarantee encryption and regulatory compliance.
Transmission of confidential data is conducted via secure channels i.e. VPNs and encrypted emails.
All confidential data are encrypted both in transit and at rest, following industry-standard encryption protocols (e.g., AES-256).
Access to storage areas containing confidential data is restricted to authorized personnel.
Access control systems i.e. keycards is used to manage physical access.
Identification:
For IT Department

System logs are records generated by operating systems, applications, or network devices that provide a detailed history of events, activities, and transactions occurring within a system
Regularly analyse system logs for unusual access patterns and failed login attempts to monitor for signs of data breaches.
For Employee

System logs are records generated by operating systems, applications, or network devices that provide a detailed history of events, activities, and transactions occurring within a system
Regularly analyse system logs for unusual access patterns and failed login attempts to monitor for signs of data breaches.
Reporting:

Employees must report any suspected data breaches immediately to their supervisor and the IT department.
An incident reporting form must be filled out and submitted to the IT department for documentation.
Escalation Protocol:
Depending on the severity, escalate incidents to management and legal counsel as necessary.

The IT Security manager will immediately isolate affected systems to prevent further unauthorized access. This team is responsible for implementing containment measures, which may include disconnecting the affected systems from the network, disabling user accounts, or restricting access until a thorough investigation is conducted and the issue is resolved.

The Incident Response Team (IRT) will conduct a thorough investigation to determine the cause and impact of the breach. They will collect relevant logs and evidence, analyse data to identify vulnerabilities, and assess the breach's extent. Interviews with personnel may be conducted for additional insights. The team will document findings and prepare an incident report with recommendations for remediation. This approach helps prevent similar incidents in the future.

Affected stakeholders will be notified via email or formal communication channels, detailing the nature of the breach, affected data, and potential risks. Guidance will include recommended actions to protect their information, such as changing passwords and monitoring for suspicious activities. Regular updates will be provided as more information becomes available.

Management and the legal team are kept informed through scheduled progress updates, including regular emails being sent on their respective official email-ids, meetings, and incident reports. All critical developments, decisions, and actions are documented and communicated in a timely manner to ensure alignment and compliance throughout the process.

Corrective actions including revising data access controls, enhancing encryption protocols, updating security policies, providing targeted employee retraining, and improving incident detection systems are take. These measures are designed to address vulnerabilities identified during the investigation and prevent similar breaches in the future.

steps.heading: Resolution and Follow-Up - Post-Incident Review

body.text: A review meeting is conducted by the Incident Response Team, led by the IT Security Manager to analyze response effectiveness and identify improvements by enhancing communication protocols, refining the incident response process and upgrading security monitoring tools.

steps.responsible: Incident Response Team, led by the IT Security Manager

body.text:
Documentation Retention: Maintain detailed records of the incident, including timelines, actions taken, and any communications for at least three years.
Regular Review: The IT Security Officer, will review and update the procedures annually or following significant incidents to ensure their effectiveness and alignment with evolving security threats and legal requirements.

blocks.text:
Documentation Retention: Maintain detailed records of the incident, including timelines, actions taken, and any communications for at least three years.
Regular Review: The IT Security Officer, will review and update the procedures annually or following significant incidents to ensure their effectiveness and alignment with evolving security threats and legal requirements.

sops.title: Securing Third-Party Data from Unauthorized Access

blocks.text: To ensure the protection of sensitive information received from or shared with third parties by applying stringent access controls, maintaining data confidentiality, and minimizing the risk of unauthorized disclosure or exposure.

body.text:
Access to sensitive third-party data is restricted to authorized personnel only.
Cherry Hill implements Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to assign access based on employees’ specific roles and responsibilities.
Access rights are reviewed periodically to ensure alignment with current job functions.
All third-party data is encrypted:

substeps.text: During transmission using secure protocols such as SSL/TLS.
At rest using encryption standards like AES-256.
Encryption keys are securely stored and are accessible only on a need-to-know basis.

body.text:
Third-party data is stored on encrypted servers with restricted access.
Regular reviews are conducted to verify access permissions and ensure compliance with internal data protection protocols.

Data is shared using encrypted emails or Secure File Transfer Protocols (SFTP).
Recipient identity and authorization are verified prior to sharing.
Audit logs are maintained for all data-sharing transactions, recording recipient details and timestamps.

All vendors or service providers with access to sensitive data are required to sign a Data Protection Agreement (DPA).
Contracts mandate:

substeps.text: Implementation of security measures equivalent to Cherry Hill’s standards.
Immediate reporting of any data breaches involving third-party information.

body.text: Cherry Hill conducts regular data protection training for employees, covering:

substeps.text: Proper handling of third-party information.
Secure sharing practices.
Legal and organizational responsibilities.
Employees are informed of potential consequences of non-compliance.

body.text:
Monitoring systems are deployed to track access and detect unauthorized attempts.
Periodic audits are performed on:

substeps.text: Access logs.
Storage and sharing practices.
Third-party contract compliance.
Identified security gaps are promptly addressed.

body.text:
In the event of a data breach involving third-party data, Cherry Hill’s Incident Response Procedure is activated.
Affected third parties are:

substeps.text: Notified without delay.
Provided with details of the breach, risks, and corrective measures undertaken.

sops.title: Stakeholder Consent and Data Processing Retention and Disposal

blocks.text: To ensure that data is handled in compliance with stakeholder permissions, maintaining appropriate data retention periods and secure disposal practices to uphold privacy standards and regulatory requirements.

body.text: Consent is obtained through formal mechanisms through signed consent form and digital agreements. These documents clearly outline the purpose of data collection, how the data will be used, and stakeholders rights. Additionally, a confirmation process through email verification and electronic signature is used to ensure stakeholders have fully understood the terms before granting their consent.

Stakeholders are provided with clear information which is communicated through a Privacy Notice which outlines how data will be used, the retention periods, and the stakeholders rights regarding their data, including access, correction, or deletion. These documents are provided at the point of data collection, either in print or digital form.

Establishing Retention Timelines: Each type of data is categorized based on its sensitivity and relevance, with specific retention timelines defined according to legal requirements, business needs, or contractual obligations.

rows: Compliance with legal requirements and identity verification
Secure shredding for physical records; cryptographic erasure for digital data
To demonstrate compliance with data protection laws
Compliance with labor laws and future reference
Secure shredding for physical records; cryptographic erasure for digital data

body.text: Tracking Retention Periods: Automated systems i.e. Microsoft SQL Server is utilized to track the retention period of stored data, ensuring that data is flagged for review or deletion once the retention period expires.

Secure Disposal: Once data is no longer required, it is securely deleted using methods appropriate to its sensitivity. For digital data, secure deletion methods such as data wiping or cryptographic erasure are used. For physical data, documents are shredded or incinerated in a controlled environment.
Compliance Checks: Regular audits are conducted to ensure that data is retained or disposed of in accordance with the established policies and legal requirements.

Regular Audits: The Data Protection Officer (DPO) will conduct the annual audits of data access and handling practices. The audit will be conducted through a systematic review process, including examining access logs, evaluating data handling procedures, interviewing relevant personnel, and assessing compliance with established policies. Additionally, random sampling of data access and handling activities may be performed to ensure adherence to standards.
Continuous Monitoring: Automated monitoring tool i.e Intrusion Detection System (IDS) to detect unauthorized access and anomalies in data access patterns.

sops.title: Audits of Control Procedure to ensure Ethical Compliance

blocks.text: To ensure Ethical Compliance is to regularly assess and verify that ethical standards and controls are effectively implemented across operations, preventing non-compliance and fostering a culture of integrity with Cherry hill.

body.text:
Audits are conducted annually or after significant organizational changes.
The Audit Team schedules audits in advance and defines specific objectives and scope.

rows: Ensure accuracy of financial statements and compliance with accounting standards.
Review of financial records, transactions, and reporting practices.
Verify adherence to procurement policies and ethical vendor selection.
Examination of vendor contracts, selection processes, and compliance documentation.
Assess compliance with labor laws and internal policies regarding employee treatment.
Review of HR records, hiring practices, and employee feedback.
Evaluate truthfulness in advertising and compliance with marketing regulations.
Analysis of marketing materials and promotional activities.
Review adherence to internal policies and procedures across operations.
Assessment of operational processes and compliance with standards.
Assess the effectiveness of information security measures and data protection.
Evaluation of IT systems, access controls, and data management practices.
Identify and mitigate risks associated with corrupt practices and bribery incidents.
Review of policies, employee training, and incident reports.

body.text:
The Audit Team reviews documentation and records related to the identified areas of ethics i.e. financial statements, vendor contracts, employee records.
Compliance with established ethical guidelines, policies, and regulatory requirements is assessed.
Interviews with key personnel are conducted to gain insights into ethical practices and any concerns.

The Audit Team analyzes collected data to identify trends, anomalies, and potential areas of ethical non-compliance.
Metrics and benchmarks are utilized to assess performance against ethical standards.

narrative.text:
Audit findings are compiled into a detailed report that highlights compliance and non-compliance areas, along with recommendations for improvement.
The report is presented to management and relevant stakeholders for review.

An action plan is developed by the Audit Team in collaboration with relevant stakeholders, such as department heads and management representatives for addressing identified issues, detailing timelines and responsible parties.
Follow-up audits are scheduled to verify the implementation of corrective actions and assess ongoing compliance.

blocks.text: All audit records, including planning documents, evaluation results, reports, and follow-up actions, are maintained for a minimum of five years by the Audit Team in conjunction with the Compliance Department.

sops.title: Procedure for Employee Compliance and Awareness

blocks.text: To ensure that all Cherry Hill employees understand and comply with data protection policies and ethical standards, fostering a culture of accountability and awareness of applicable regulations.

body.text: All employees must complete compliance training on data protection, confidentiality, and information security:

At the time of onboarding
Annually thereafter
Training topics include:

substeps.text: Cherry Hill's data protection policies
Secure handling of sensitive information
Identification of phishing and cybersecurity threats
Breach reporting and response procedures

body.text:
Updated training materials and handbooks are distributed to all employees.
Materials are reviewed periodically to ensure compliance with current laws and best practices.

Periodic initiatives such as newsletters, posters, and team briefings reinforce key concepts.
Simulated phishing exercises are conducted to evaluate employee awareness, with feedback provided for improvement.
Employees are encouraged to report any data protection concerns or suspicious activities without fear of retaliation.

Email: ethics.compliance@cherryhill.in
Contact Person: Data Protection Officer

Records of training completion and participation are maintained.
Program effectiveness is assessed through employee feedback, and necessary improvements are made.

The Data Protection Officer conducts audits to evaluate compliance and identify gaps.
Findings are documented, and corrective actions are implemented accordingly.

responsibilities: Complete all mandatory training programs.
Report suspected breaches or concerns via the designated channels.
Ensure team compliance with SOPs and training participation.
Support the reporting and resolution of data protection issues.
Oversee implementation and enforcement of data protection measures.
Conduct audits and serve as the main contact for incident reporting.
Maintain and monitor data security systems.
Investigate incidents and implement preventive technical measures.

narrative.text:
The DPO will conduct regular audits to ensure adherence.
The IT Manager will track employee training participation and follow up with defaulters.

blocks.text:
Non-compliance may result in disciplinary action, depending on the severity:
Verbal/written warnings
Suspension
Termination of employment
Disciplinary actions are managed by HR in coordination with relevant departments.

The SOP is reviewed annually by the DPO.
Emergency reviews are conducted if laws or internal processes change significantly.
All revisions are documented and shared with employees for acknowledgment.

This SOP outlines the procedures and responsibilities for the systematic inspection of all machinery and equipment used in operations at Cherry Hill. The purpose is to ensure safe working conditions, prevent equipment-related accidents, maintain compliance with local and international safety standards, and reduce downtime due to equipment failure. Regular inspections help identify wear, malfunction, or safety risks early, allowing timely corrective actions.

This SOP applies to all equipment and machinery used across Cherry Hill Interiors' project sites, workshops, and offices. It includes tools and equipment such as power drills, cutting machines, welding equipment, scaffolding, ladders, and all other operational equipment used in interior fit-out and construction activities.

responsibilities: Oversees the implementation of equipment safety inspections, ensures compliance with national regulations and client safety requirements, and reports audit findings to management.
Conducts scheduled inspections, completes inspection checklists, addresses issues promptly, and maintains comprehensive inspection records.
Perform basic pre-use visual checks, promptly report any abnormalities or malfunctions, and participate in ongoing safety training sessions.

body.text: Operators visually check equipment before use, looking for signs of damage, loose wires, leaks, or abnormal noises.
Maintenance staff conduct functional checks on moving parts, belts, motors, and control panels, focusing on wear and potential hazards.
Detailed inspections are carried out by qualified personnel, covering electrical systems, mechanical integrity, and safety interlocks.
A full audit is conducted involving external or senior internal experts to ensure alignment with company compliance and global client standards.
Operators check that all safety features—such as emergency stops, guard covers, and foot pedals—are functional. Any irregularity is recorded in the daily logbook and reported to the supervisor.
Maintenance personnel inspect pressure gauges, wiring insulation, control switches, and machine guards. Calibration of sensitive equipment is verified, and any repairs are initiated.

Comprehensive review of structural elements, alarm systems, sensor functions, and safety relays. All findings are documented in the Equipment Safety Inspection Form, which is updated after each inspection cycle and stored for records and audit reference.

blocks.text: All inspection records, including the Equipment Safety Inspection Form, are maintained digitally for five years. Each record includes:

Date and type of inspection
Inspector's name and designation
Equipment ID or location
Observations and test results
Actions taken and resolution timelines
These records are available for internal audits and buyer verifications.

Any equipment with safety risks is immediately tagged as "Do Not Use" and removed from operation.
Maintenance follows up with repairs or replacement, based on manufacturer recommendations.
Critical faults are escalated to the Safety Officer and Production Head for resolution and tracking.
All operators and maintenance staff are trained in basic equipment safety, use of personal protective equipment (PPE), and emergency procedures.

Refresher training is conducted annually.
Additional training is given when new machinery is installed or when changes are made to existing equipment.
Internal safety audits are conducted periodically by the Safety Officer and reviewed by the Compliance Team.

Findings are documented and tracked until closure.
Non-compliance issues are analyzed, and preventive measures are implemented.
Audit results are also shared during client audits or third-party safety inspections.

This SOP is reviewed annually or whenever new equipment is added, safety regulations are updated, or significant process changes occur. The Safety Officer is responsible for initiating the review, and updates are approved by senior management to ensure ongoing effectiveness and compliance.

Cherry Hill Interiors Pvt. Ltd. is committed to providing and maintaining a safe, healthy, and secure working environment for all employees, contractors, subcontractors, and visitors across its offices, manufacturing facility, warehouses, and project sites. Considering the nature of interior fit-out, civil, electrical, HVAC, and MEP activities, workplace safety is integrated into every stage of project planning and execution. This procedure establishes standard workplace safety practices to identify hazards, minimize occupational risks, prevent incidents, and ensure compliance with applicable legal requirements and client safety standards.

To establish standardized workplace safety practices that promote safe working conditions, prevent workplace injuries and occupational illnesses, ensure compliance with health and safety requirements, and encourage a proactive safety culture across all Cherry Hill operations.

This procedure applies to all Cherry Hill offices, manufacturing facilities, warehouses, project sites, and temporary work locations. It is applicable to all employees, contract workers, subcontractors, consultants, suppliers, and visitors engaged in company activities.

responsibilities: Ensure workplace safety requirements are incorporated into project planning and monitor compliance throughout project execution.
Conduct safety inspections, risk assessments, incident investigations, and awareness programmes while monitoring implementation of workplace safety practices.
Ensure safe work practices are followed, conduct daily toolbox talks, verify PPE compliance, and immediately address unsafe conditions.
Follow all safety procedures, wear required PPE, report hazards or incidents promptly, and participate in mandatory safety training.

substeps.text: Conduct a site-specific Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) before commencement of work.
Prepare a Site Safety Plan identifying major hazards, emergency arrangements, and control measures.
Ensure required permits, statutory approvals, and emergency contact details are available before mobilization.
Identify high-risk activities such as work at height, hot work, lifting operations, and electrical work and implement appropriate controls.
Provide mandatory safety induction to all employees, contractors, and visitors before entering the workplace or project site.
Conduct daily toolbox talks before the commencement of work to discuss hazards, control measures, and safety precautions.
Provide periodic refresher training on emergency response, PPE usage, fire safety, electrical safety, manual handling, and safe work practices.
Maintain attendance records for all safety training and awareness programmes.
Provide appropriate PPE based on job-specific hazards and work activities.
Ensure mandatory use of safety helmets, safety shoes, reflective jackets, gloves, safety goggles, and other PPE wherever applicable.
Inspect PPE regularly and replace damaged or expired equipment immediately.
Supervisors shall monitor PPE compliance during routine workplace inspections.
Ensure all tools, machinery, and electrical equipment are inspected before use and are maintained in safe working condition.
Restrict unauthorized access to hazardous work areas through barricading and safety signage.
Obtain the necessary Permit to Work (PTW) before carrying out hot work, confined space entry, electrical isolation, or work at height.
Follow approved lifting techniques and use suitable lifting equipment for handling heavy materials.
Maintain clearly identified emergency exits, assembly points, and evacuation routes at all workplaces.
Ensure fire extinguishers, first aid kits, emergency lighting, and other emergency equipment are readily accessible and periodically inspected.
Display emergency contact numbers at prominent locations.
Conduct emergency evacuation and fire drills periodically to assess preparedness and improve response effectiveness.
Report all accidents, injuries, near misses, unsafe acts, and unsafe conditions immediately to the Site Supervisor or HSE Team.
Investigate all reported incidents to determine root causes and identify corrective and preventive actions.
Record incidents and monitor the implementation of corrective actions until closure.
Communicate lessons learned from incidents to employees and contractors to prevent recurrence.
Conduct daily workplace inspections to identify unsafe conditions and verify compliance with safety requirements.
Carry out periodic HSE audits across project sites and operational facilities.
Track corrective actions arising from inspections and audits until satisfactory closure.
Review safety performance indicators, including incident frequency, near misses, inspection findings, and training completion, to identify opportunities for continual improvement.

steps.heading: Ergonomics and Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI) Prevention

substeps.text: Employees shall maintain proper workstation ergonomics, including correct chair height, monitor position, and keyboard placement to reduce the risk of Repetitive Strain Injuries (RSIs).
Employees performing prolonged desk-based work shall take short stretching or movement breaks at regular intervals to minimize muscle fatigue and discomfort.
Ergonomic assessments shall be conducted periodically, and appropriate ergonomic accessories shall be provided where required.
Employees experiencing symptoms such as pain, numbness, or discomfort shall promptly report them to their supervisor or the HSE Team for appropriate action.
Keep floors and walkways clean, dry, and free from spills, debris, and obstructions.
Ensure adequate lighting and use anti-slip mats where necessary.
Use handrails on stairs and only approved ladders or platforms for working at height.
Wear slip-resistant safety footwear in operational and project areas.
Report and rectify damaged flooring or other trip hazards promptly.

blocks.text: This Workplace Safety Practices Procedure shall be reviewed annually by the HSE Team in consultation with the Project Management and Operations departments. The review shall consider workplace incidents, inspection findings, employee feedback, legal updates, and changes in operational activities. Where necessary, the procedure shall be revised to strengthen workplace safety controls and support Cherry Hill's commitment to continual improvement in health and safety performance.

To establish a standardized procedure for identifying, providing, inspecting, maintaining, and monitoring emergency equipment across Cherry Hill Interiors Pvt. Ltd. to ensure prompt response during emergencies, minimize potential risks, and protect employees, contractors, visitors, and company assets.

This procedure applies to all Cherry Hill offices, warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and project sites. It covers emergency equipment required for fire protection, first aid, emergency evacuation, spill response, and other emergency situations arising from workplace activities.

responsibilities: Identify emergency equipment requirements, conduct inspections, maintain records, and coordinate servicing and emergency drills.
Ensure emergency equipment is available, accessible, and properly maintained within their respective work areas.
Be aware of the location and proper use of emergency equipment, report any deficiencies, and participate in emergency drills and training.

body.text: Based on workplace hazards and operational requirements, the following emergency equipment shall be provided where applicable:

Fire extinguishers, fire alarm systems, smoke detectors, and fire hose reels.
First aid kits and emergency medical supplies.
Emergency exit signage and emergency lighting.
Spill response kits for paints, adhesives, fuels, and other hazardous substances.
Eye wash stations where hazardous chemicals are handled.
Emergency contact information, evacuation maps, and designated assembly point signage.

steps.heading: Identification and Provision of Emergency Equipment

body.text:
Conduct workplace risk assessments to identify the type, quantity, and location of emergency equipment required based on workplace hazards and operational activities.
Install emergency equipment before commencement of operations at offices, warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and project sites.
Position emergency equipment at clearly identified, easily accessible, and unobstructed locations with appropriate safety signage.
Maintain an Emergency Equipment Register containing equipment type, identification number, location, inspection frequency, service due date, and responsible person.
Review emergency equipment requirements whenever there are significant changes in workplace layout, project activities, or identified risks.

Inspect emergency equipment at scheduled intervals to verify its accessibility, condition, functionality, and compliance with applicable requirements.
Check fire extinguishers, first aid kits, emergency lighting, alarms, spill kits, and other emergency equipment for damage, expiry, or operational readiness.
Arrange servicing, refilling, repair, calibration, or replacement of defective or expired equipment through authorized service providers, where applicable.
Ensure emergency equipment remains free from obstruction and is readily available for immediate use.
Replenish or replace any emergency equipment used during an emergency, incident, or mock drill before normal operations resume.
Record all inspections, maintenance activities, servicing, and replacements for future reference.

Provide employees, contractors, and visitors with information on the location and use of emergency equipment during induction programmes.
Conduct periodic awareness sessions on the safe use of fire extinguishers, first aid kits, spill response equipment, and emergency evacuation procedures.
Conduct mock drills at planned intervals to verify emergency preparedness and familiarize personnel with emergency response procedures.
Display emergency response instructions, emergency contact numbers, evacuation routes, and assembly point information at prominent locations.

Monitor the adequacy and effectiveness of emergency equipment through routine inspections, internal audits, and emergency drills.
Investigate any deficiencies or failures identified during inspections or emergency situations and implement corrective actions promptly.
Periodically review emergency equipment requirements to ensure they remain suitable for operational activities, workplace hazards, and legal requirements.
Track corrective actions until completion and verify their effectiveness during subsequent inspections.

sops.title: Information security due diligence program on third parties

blocks.text: This SOP establishes the framework for conducting information security due diligence on third parties engaged by Cherry Hill Interiors Pvt. Ltd. The objective is to evaluate the information security practices of suppliers, contractors, consultants, service providers, and business partners to safeguard confidential information, protect business systems, and minimize risks associated with third-party engagements.
This procedure applies to all third parties that access, process, store, transmit, or manage Cherry Hill's confidential information or information systems, including:

Suppliers providing products or services to the company.
Contractors and subcontractors working at offices, warehouses, manufacturing facilities, or project sites.
IT service providers, cloud service providers, and software vendors.
Consultants and business partners handling confidential business or customer information.
This SOP applies to all third-party engagements before onboarding and throughout the business relationship.

body.text:
All new suppliers, contractors, consultants, and service providers shall undergo an information security due diligence assessment before engagement.
Third parties shall be identified based on the nature of services provided, level of access to company information, and potential information security risks.
The Procurement Department shall coordinate with the concerned department to determine whether information security due diligence is required.

Third parties shall be categorized based on the level of information security risk associated with their services.

The assessment shall consider:

Type and sensitivity of information accessed.
Access to company IT systems, applications, or confidential documents.
Criticality of services provided.
Previous information security incidents or regulatory non-compliance.
Risk Levels

Low Risk: Limited or no access to confidential information or company systems.
Medium Risk: Access to internal business information or selected company systems.
High Risk: Access to confidential business information, customer information, critical systems, or cloud-based services.
The following due diligence activities shall be completed before onboarding:

Review the supplier's information security policies, procedures, and internal controls.
Evaluate data protection practices, access control mechanisms, password management, and incident response arrangements.
Verify compliance with applicable legal, contractual, and customer information security requirements.
Obtain completed supplier information security questionnaires and supporting documents where applicable.
Review previous security incidents, data breaches, or regulatory actions that may affect the supplier's risk profile.

Cherry Hill shall conduct supplier on-site assessments, where applicable, as part of the information security due diligence programme.
The assessment shall verify the implementation of physical and information security controls at the supplier's premises.
The assessment may include verification of:

Physical access controls and visitor management.
Protection of confidential documents and records.
Secure storage of electronic devices and information.
User access management and password controls.
Data backup and recovery practices.
Employee awareness of information security requirements.
Any observations or non-conformities identified during the assessment shall be documented, and corrective actions shall be communicated to the supplier for timely closure.

Information security and confidentiality requirements shall be incorporated into supplier agreements, purchase orders, or service contracts, wherever applicable.
Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) shall be executed where confidential or proprietary information is shared.
High-risk suppliers shall be approved only after completion of the due diligence assessment and closure of any significant observations.

High-risk suppliers shall be reviewed periodically to verify continued compliance with Cherry Hill's information security requirements.
Supplier performance shall be monitored through contract reviews, audits, incident reports, customer feedback, and periodic supplier evaluations.
Information security due diligence shall be repeated whenever there are significant changes in the supplier's services, ownership, information systems, or identified security risks.
Corrective actions arising from supplier assessments shall be monitored until satisfactory closure.

responsibilities: Conduct information security assessments, review security controls, and monitor compliance.
Ensure due diligence is completed before supplier onboarding and maintain assessment records.
Participate in supplier evaluations and identify information security risks relevant to their functions.
Cooperate during assessments, provide requested information, and implement agreed corrective actions.

blocks.text: This SOP shall be reviewed annually, or whenever there are significant changes in information security requirements, applicable regulations, business operations, or third-party risks. Findings from supplier assessments, security incidents, internal audits, and management reviews shall be incorporated to continually improve the effectiveness of the Information Security Due Diligence Programme.

sops.title: Anti-corruption due diligence program on third parties

blocks.text: This SOP establishes the framework for conducting anti-corruption due diligence on third parties engaged by Cherry Hill Interiors Pvt. Ltd. The objective is to identify and mitigate bribery and corruption risks, promote ethical business practices, and ensure that all third-party engagements comply with applicable anti-corruption laws, company policies, and contractual obligations.
This procedure applies to all third parties engaged by Cherry Hill Interiors Pvt. Ltd., including:

Suppliers of materials, furniture, fixtures, and equipment.
Contractors and subcontractors working on project sites.
Consultants, architects, designers, and project management firms.
Service providers, agents, logistics providers, and business partners.
This SOP applies to all new third-party engagements and periodic reviews of existing third-party relationships.

body.text:
All new suppliers, contractors, consultants, and business partners shall undergo anti-corruption due diligence before engagement.
The Procurement Department shall identify third parties requiring assessment based on the nature of services, contract value, business relationship, and potential corruption risks.
Existing suppliers may also be reassessed whenever significant changes occur in their operations or contractual arrangements.

Third parties shall be classified according to their corruption risk profile.

The assessment shall consider:

Nature of goods or services provided.
Contract value and strategic importance.
Geographic location and corruption risk of the operating region.
Previous history of legal, ethical, or regulatory violations.
Level of interaction with government authorities or regulatory bodies on behalf of Cherry Hill.
Risk Levels

Low Risk: Routine suppliers with limited corruption exposure.
Medium Risk: Contractors and service providers involved in significant operational activities.
High Risk: Third parties engaged in high-value contracts, government-related projects, or operating in higher-risk jurisdictions.
The following due diligence activities shall be completed before onboarding:

Verify the third party's business registration, ownership structure, and legal status.
Review the supplier's code of conduct, ethics policy, or anti-corruption practices, where available.
Obtain completed supplier due diligence questionnaires and supporting documentation.
Review any previous legal proceedings, regulatory sanctions, fraud, bribery, or corruption-related allegations.
Assess any actual or potential conflicts of interest that may affect the business relationship.

Cherry Hill may conduct supplier on-site assessments as part of its anti-corruption due diligence programme, based on the supplier's risk level and business criticality.

The assessment may include verification of:

Business operations and management practices.
Implementation of ethical business controls.
Compliance with anti-bribery and anti-corruption requirements.
Record-keeping and supporting documentation related to business transactions.
Awareness of employees regarding ethical business practices.
Any observations or non-conformities identified during the assessment shall be documented, and corrective actions shall be communicated to the supplier for timely implementation.

Anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and ethical business conduct requirements shall be incorporated into supplier agreements and service contracts, where applicable.
Suppliers shall be required to comply with Cherry Hill's Supplier Code of Conduct and applicable legal requirements.
High-risk suppliers shall be approved only after satisfactory completion of the due diligence assessment and closure of significant observations.

Supplier performance shall be monitored through periodic supplier evaluations, contract reviews, audits, and feedback received during project execution.
High-risk suppliers may be reassessed periodically or whenever significant changes occur in ownership, management, business operations, or identified corruption risks.
Any reported allegations of bribery, fraud, unethical conduct, or regulatory non-compliance involving third parties shall be investigated, and appropriate corrective actions shall be implemented.
Corrective actions arising from supplier assessments or investigations shall be monitored until satisfactory closure.

responsibilities: Conduct third-party due diligence before supplier onboarding and maintain assessment records.
Review due diligence findings, assess corruption risks, and approve high-risk engagements.
Participate in supplier evaluations and report any unethical practices or conflicts of interest.
Cooperate during due diligence assessments, provide requested information, and comply with Cherry Hill's anti-corruption requirements.

blocks.text: This SOP shall be reviewed annually, or whenever there are significant changes in applicable anti-corruption regulations, business operations, or supplier risk profiles. Findings from supplier assessments, audits, investigations, and management reviews shall be considered to continually strengthen Cherry Hill's Anti-Corruption Due Diligence Programme.

This SOP establishes the process followed by Cherry Hill Interiors Pvt. Ltd. to maintain adequate safety stock of critical materials and consumables to minimize supply disruptions, support timely project execution, and ensure business continuity.

This procedure applies to all warehouses, stores, and project sites of Cherry Hill Interiors Pvt. Ltd. and covers critical materials, consumables, and project-specific items that require safety stock based on operational requirements.

responsibilities: Maintain safety stock levels and ensure timely replenishment of critical materials.
Monitor inventory levels, maintain stock records, and notify Procurement when stock reaches the reorder level.
Communicate project material requirements and expected demand to support inventory planning.

substeps.text: Cherry Hill identifies critical materials that are essential for uninterrupted project execution.
Safety stock requirements are determined based on historical consumption, supplier lead time, project schedules, and business-critical requirements.
The list of safety stock items is reviewed periodically and updated whenever operational requirements change.
Minimum stock levels and reorder levels are established for identified critical materials.
Procurement plans material purchases to maintain the required safety stock and reduce the risk of stock shortages.
Where feasible, approved alternate suppliers are identified for critical materials to improve supply continuity.
Inventory levels are monitored regularly through stock registers or the inventory management system.
When inventory reaches the established reorder level, the Stores Team raises a material replenishment request to Procurement.
Procurement initiates purchase orders to replenish stock before inventory falls below the minimum safety stock level.
Any anticipated supply delays or shortages are communicated to the concerned Project Manager so that appropriate mitigation measures can be implemented.
Safety stock materials are stored in designated locations with proper identification and inventory records.
Periodic physical stock verification is conducted to ensure inventory accuracy.
Materials are issued following the First-In, First-Out (FIFO) principle, wherever applicable, to minimize damage, deterioration, or expiry.
Damaged, obsolete, or excess materials are identified separately and managed in accordance with the company's inventory control procedures.

blocks.text: This procedure shall be reviewed annually or whenever there are significant changes in project activities, inventory management practices, supplier performance, or business continuity requirements. Feedback from inventory reviews and operational teams shall be incorporated to ensure the continued effectiveness of the Safety Stock Procedure.
